message.content: {"caption":"A workflow diagram shows how paired task executions guide skill edits, while a verifier checks the resulting candidate against explicit constraints.","description":"Three rounded panels run from left to right. In Setup, “T·W·S₀” denotes the task, workspace, and initial skill. The Task Interpreter reads explicit constraints from T. The Task-Compiled Verifier is compiled once from T and locked. Matched-run setup keeps T and W and the agent π frozen, varying only whether skill S is loaded. Its connection leads to the paired executions in the center: an agent run “with Skill S” (τw) and a run “without Skill” (τwo). The robot icons denote these agent executions. The paired runs feed the PACE comparison, whose four listed dimensions are Process Adherence, Artifact Evidence, Consistency, and Effectiveness Delta. A downward arrow leads from these criteria to “PACE output,” which marks passages to edit or protect; the first pair locks the choice of Refine or Repair. A separate “Verifier check” checks explicit task constraints. Connector lines carry the PACE output and verifier-check results toward the Edit and check panel. At its top, “verdict → action” maps “helped → edit,” “inert → defer,” and “hurt → reject.” Below a dashed divider, the Skill Iterator offers Refine, shown with a filter icon: preserve the working workflow and delete, clarify, or correct local defects; and Repair, shown with a wrench: replace conflicting procedures and add missing execution information. The bottom feedback path labels a “candidate skill S′” and loops it back toward comparison and checking; the output at right is “evolved skill S*.” No check or cross marks are shown.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
